actions.description: Advance the simulated world by a bounded number of fixed timesteps, optionally applying an action for each step, and return the resulting observation and terminal flags.

inputs.name: ticks

actions.description: Reset the simulated world to a scenario start state and return the initial observation. When a seed is supplied the endpoint records it in the receipt; otherwise the endpoint's declared default seed applies.

inputs.description: Seed for World.seed(); RobotEnv.reset() itself takes no arguments
inputs.name: seed

actions.name: reset

actions.description: Set the seed used by the simulated world's random number generators for subsequent steps, without resetting the world. The accepted seed is echoed in the receipt.

facts.text: The environment is registered as gripper-env-v0 with entry point manipulation_main.gripperEnv.robot:RobotEnv
RobotEnv requires a config argument; a path is loaded as YAML before World is constructed
The continuous, non-simplified action space is Box(-1, 1, shape=(5,))
The five action components are translation xyz, yaw rotation and the gripper open/close signal
The full action clips the translation norm to max_translation and the yaw to max_yaw_rotation, both taken from the config
A positive fifth action value opens the gripper when it is closed, a negative one closes it when it is open, and otherwise the robot moves
In non-simplified depth mode _observe stacks the depth image with a zero pad whose [0][0] carries the actuator state
The non-simplified depth observation space is Box(0, 255, shape=(height, width, 2))
The upstream tests expect Box(-1, 1, shape=(5,)) for the continuous case and a (64, 64, 2) observation for the non-simplified depth case
step returns (obs, reward, done, info) and reports done when episode_step equals time_horizon - 1
World advances the physics by 1/240 s in every step_sim call
World.seed seeds the random generator with gym.utils.seeding.np_random and evaluate mode fixes RandomState(1)
The gripper width is measured from 0.05 per finger, so a fully open gripper is 0.1 wide
The upstream dependencies include gym 0.19.0, pybullet 3.2.5, tensorflow 1.14.0 and numpy 1.18

determinism.notes: reset(seed) or cap.world.seed.v1 fixes the random object position of the fake's next reset and the kinematic update is deterministic, so the same seed and actions repeat a trajectory; upstream seeds numpy's generator through World.seed (simulation.py:91-100), the fake uses Python's random.Random, so one seed does not give the same trajectory on the two

gaps: the deployed fake is kinematic: it has no pybullet rigid-body scene, contacts, friction, gravity, actuator or sensor model (simulation.py:43-44); the upstream RobotEnv.step also runs an actuator settling loop and one 1/240 s physics step (robot.py:159-180), while the fake advances one tick

the fake returns an 8 x 8 x 2 depth-plus-actuator stand-in; the real observation space is 64 x 64 x 2 (tests_gripper/test_sim.py:39-40, config/camera_info.yaml:1-2) and there is no rendered depth image
there is no TensorFlow encoder and no camera model; the depth channel is an analytic placeholder, not the upstream RGBDSensor output (sensor.py:36-41, robot.py:190-205)
the reward is a constant 0.0 and the episode ends at a stand-in horizon of 150 ticks; the upstream reward functions and the config's time_horizon are not modelled (rewards.py:25-52)
reset starts one fixed kinematic scene; it does not retry until an object is inside the camera field of view (robot.py:19-30) and the scene objects are not modelled
no wall-clock pacing: realtime_factor 0, and the fake's timestep is nominally the upstream 1/240 s physics step, not the duration of one RobotEnv.step call
the fake was not compared with the upstream environment: the upstream package needs gym 0.19.0, pybullet 3.2.5 and tensorflow 1.14.0 (setup.py:6-24) and was neither installed nor imported
snapshot and restore are not offered: RobotEnv exposes no get_state or set_state
no physical device is modelled and the model was never validated against one

measures.description: Last observation (derived from the observation space)
measures.name: observation

safe_state.description: the simulation stops advancing: after an e-stop no step or reset is accepted until mhs.safety.reset clears the latch; the environment state is kept and stays readable
